messages:
maya: quick heads-up — during a small canary this morning we started seeing a weird regression on embeds: higher 95th latency and a few 413s for mixed-dim payloads. not blaming runtime yet, but want to sync on routing/console UX before we widen the rollout.

alex: saw that too. sample from logs: `POST /v1/embeddings` with payload containing 1 x 1024-dim + 5 x 768-dim vectors. runtime returned 413 with no guidance.

kevin: do we have preflight enabled for the canary? i thought the preflight middleware would have returned a structured hint.

maya: preflight was on, but the preflight response was a generic `oversize` for that tenant. the issue: splitter couldn't find an efficient split plan because mixed dims + bytes budget. it fell back to fastfail.

tess: hmm. is the splitter using bytes-only heuristic? we recently pushed the byte-budget first pass in the router to avoid extra compute. mixed dims trip that a lot.

alex: yeah that's the thing — many clients pack varied-dim embeddings in one request. routing needs a better contract. suggestion: preflight should surface `suggested_split` and `unit_estimate` fields so client/console show a clear remediation. e.g.:

```
{
  "oversize": true,
  "unit_estimate": "6.4-7.1 units",
  "suggested_split": ["split by dims", "max_per_chunk: 3"],
  "quota_hint": "use-dedicated or increase per-request-bytes"
}
```

kevin: love that. console UX could surface that as a one-click `split request` helper where devs can preview chunking. also for telemetry we should tag the preflight failure with `split_strategy: none|bytes|dims` and `tenant_shares`.

maya: +1. also thinking about routing policy: when mixed dims are detected, we should route to an "adaptive-split" lane that can do cheap per-tenant sharding before batching into the main path. keeps latency bound.

tess: implementation note — adaptive-split lane needs a fast path op that avoids full KV cache warmups. otherwise we lose the latency gains. maybe a lighter-weight execution mode with `cache=false` and a reduced kv-reservation.

alex: operationally, we need metrics: count(preflight_oversize), pct(split_suggested_accepted), post-split latency p50/p95, and a distribution of `unit_estimate` per-tenant. also surface examples in the console: show the actual request (sanitized) and the split plan the router would apply.

kevin: one more: quota model. current per-tenant quota is bytes-based -> leads to surprises for mixed dims. propose adding "embed-units" as a first-class quota unit in the console and billing. we'd compute units = sum(dims / base_dim) * weight. base_dim could be 768. then console can show soft caps and auto-suggest quantization profiles.

maya: agree — that solves the UX mismatch. but migration: we need a rollout plan so existing customers aren't shocked. proposal: opt-in header `X-Embed-Unit-OptIn: v1` and a console toggle per-tenant. start with telemetry-only for 2 weeks.

tess: for canary, add a `preflight_verbose=true` param so preflight returns sample split details and an estimated token/time cost. we can collect anonymized samples to validate unit formula.

ingress-bot: deploybot: canary deployed to clusters eng-canary-2 at 2024-05-14T08:12Z. health check: OK. routing-config: `adaptive_split: off` in canary.

alex: ingress-bot — can you flip `adaptive_split: on` for a single tenant we own so we can test end-to-end?

ingress-bot: deploybot: toggled `adaptive_split`=on for tenant `redwood-internal` on eng-canary-2.

kevin: runbook bits: if we start seeing regression, fallback to `split-to-client` where preflight returns an explicit list of chunks and we reply 200 with `partial_accept` so clients can retry split locally. reduces pressure on runtime.

maya: action items: 1) alex to draft preflight response schema (incl fields above) by EOD. 2) tess to prototype adaptive-split fast-path (cache=false) and run microbenchmarks. 3) kevin to add telemetry events & console mockups for unit quotas. 4) ops: flip opt-in header for a friend tenant and collect 14 days of telemetry.

alex: will add schema and sample UI messages. quick Q: do we want `suggested_split` to include exact chunk boundaries or just heuristics? my vote: heuristics — we avoid binding router to client's exact packing.

kevin: heuristics + an optional `client_payload_hint` that the client can return to ask router to do precise packing server-side. keeps flexibility.

tess: ok. i'll run perf tests with 1k mixed-dim requests and report p50/p95 and cost delta.

maya: thanks everyone. let's sync in tomorrow's eng-platform standup if we have initial data. :thumbsup:
